questions.question: 限流服务所依赖的 Redis 挂了。按文章，下面哪一层限流应该 fail-close（拒绝放行）？
options: 所有层都应 fail-close，以确保绝对安全
免费层「每月 1000 次调用」的计费配额层
防御 DDoS、保护整体可用性的那一层
按 IP 限制匿名爬虫请求频率的那一层
questions.explanation: 默认 fail-open，免得限流故障变成业务故障；但计费配额超额等于公司亏钱，宁可拒也不能放，这类层要 fail-close。实战分层是抗 DDoS 层 fail-open 保命、计费配额层 fail-close 保钱，两层独立部署；全部 fail-close 会让限流故障拖垮全站。
questions.question_en: The Redis instance behind a rate limiter goes down. According to the article, which layer should fail closed (reject traffic)?
options_en: Every layer should fail closed to guarantee absolute safety
The billing-quota layer enforcing a free tier's 1,000 calls per month
The layer defending against DDoS and protecting overall availability
The layer throttling anonymous scrapers' request rate by IP
questions.explanation_en: The default is fail-open so a limiter outage doesn't become a business outage; but exceeding billing quotas loses the company money, so that layer should fail closed. In practice the anti-DDoS layer fails open to stay alive and the billing layer fails closed to protect revenue, deployed separately; failing closed everywhere would let a limiter fault take down the whole site.

questions.question: 过载时 1000 个客户端都收到 429 和「Retry-After: 30」，30 秒后同时重试，再次压垮服务。按文章，最直接的对策是？
options: 把 Retry-After 统一延长到 300 秒，给服务更充分的恢复时间
改为返回 503，让客户端按照服务端故障的语义来处理重试
给 Retry-After 加随机抖动，或让 SDK 在退避时加 jitter
取消 Retry-After 头，让客户端自行决定什么时候重新发起
questions.explanation: 所有人拿到同一个固定值就会齐步重试，造成惊群；服务端返回带随机抖动的值或客户端 SDK 加 jitter，把重试时刻打散。统一延长只是把惊群推迟；429 与 503 语义不同，错用会误导重试；去掉 Retry-After 会让客户端死循环重试。
questions.question_en: During overload, 1,000 clients all get a 429 with 'Retry-After: 30', retry in unison 30 seconds later, and knock the service over again. According to the article, what's the most direct fix?
options_en: Raise Retry-After to 300 seconds for everyone to give the service more time to recover
Return 503 instead so clients handle retries with server-failure semantics
Add random jitter to Retry-After, or have SDKs add jitter when backing off
Drop the Retry-After header and let clients decide on their own when to retry
questions.explanation_en: Identical fixed values make everyone retry in lockstep, a thundering herd; jittered values from the server or jitter in client SDKs spread the retries out. A uniformly longer wait just postpones the herd, 429 and 503 mean different things and misusing them misleads retry logic, and dropping Retry-After invites tight retry loops.

questions.question: 按文章，一个单 key 限额 100 req/s 的令牌桶，capacity 与 refill rate 应该怎么理解和设置？
options: capacity 是允许的突发大小，rate 是长期平均速率，二者按下游承受力分开设
refill rate 应设为 capacity 的十倍，让令牌桶更快地恢复到满额
两者都直接设为 100 最合理，这样就能严格保证每秒不超过 100 个请求
capacity 越大越好，这样正常用户的任何突发流量都不会被拒绝
questions.explanation: cap=100 意味着攒满后可以瞬间发 100 个请求，1ms 内瞬时 QPS 就是 10 万，可能打爆下游。cap 由下游能扛多大瞬时 burst 决定，常见为 rate × 1~3；rate 是合同，cap 是仁慈。极端场景才设 cap = rate 让流量严格匀速。
questions.question_en: According to the article, how should you understand and set capacity and refill rate for a token bucket with a per-key limit of 100 req/s?
options_en: Capacity is the allowed burst size, rate is the long-run average; set them separately based on what downstream can absorb
Refill rate should be ten times capacity so the bucket returns to full more quickly
Setting both to 100 is most sensible, since it strictly guarantees no more than 100 requests in any second
The bigger the capacity the better, so no burst from a normal user is ever rejected
questions.explanation_en: With cap=100, a full bucket can fire 100 requests at once, which over 1ms is an instantaneous 100,000 QPS and can swamp downstream. Capacity should reflect the burst downstream can absorb, commonly 1 to 3 times the rate; the rate is the contract, the capacity is the grace. Only in extreme cases is cap set equal to rate to force a strictly even flow.
